examInfo.title: JAMB History Practice Questions
examInfo.subject: History
examInfo.instructions: Choose the correct option from A-D for each question.

questions.question: The Berlin Conference of 1884-1885 was organized to
questions.explanation: The Berlin Conference was convened to regulate European colonization and trade in Africa during the New Imperialism period.

questions.question: The ancient kingdom of Kush was located in
questions.explanation: The Kingdom of Kush was an ancient African kingdom situated on the Nile River in what is now northern Sudan.

questions.question: The Trans-Atlantic slave trade was officially abolished by Britain in
questions.explanation: Britain abolished the slave trade (not slavery itself) in 1807 with the Slave Trade Act, though slavery in British colonies continued until 1833.

questions.question: The Sokoto Caliphate was founded by
questions.explanation: Usman dan Fodio founded the Sokoto Caliphate in 1804 after leading a successful jihad in northern Nigeria.

questions.question: The Great Depression began in
questions.explanation: The Great Depression began with the Wall Street Crash in October 1929 and lasted through the 1930s.

questions.question: The first European to reach India by sea was
questions.explanation: Vasco da Gama was the first European to reach India by sailing around Africa, arriving in Calicut in 1498.

questions.question: Nigeria gained independence from Britain in
questions.explanation: Nigeria gained independence from British colonial rule on October 1, 1960.

questions.question: The Cold War was primarily between
questions.explanation: The Cold War (1947-1991) was a period of geopolitical tension between the United States and the Soviet Union and their respective allies.

questions.question: The Benin Empire was famous for its
questions.explanation: The Benin Empire was renowned for its sophisticated bronze sculptures and plaques, which are now displayed in museums worldwide.

questions.question: The Scramble for Africa took place during the
questions.explanation: The Scramble for Africa occurred in the late 19th century (1880s-1914) when European powers rapidly colonized African territories.

questions.question: The Maji Maji Rebellion occurred in
questions.explanation: The Maji Maji Rebellion (1905-1907) was an armed resistance by indigenous peoples against German colonial rule in German East Africa (now Tanzania).

questions.question: The Renaissance began in
questions.explanation: The Renaissance began in Italy in the 14th century, starting in cities like Florence, Venice, and Rome.

questions.question: The Ashanti Empire was located in present-day
questions.explanation: The Ashanti Empire was a powerful West African state located in what is now Ghana, with its capital at Kumasi.

questions.question: World War I ended in
questions.explanation: World War I ended on November 11, 1918, with the signing of the Armistice between Germany and the Allied forces.

questions.question: The ancient city of Timbuktu was a center of
questions.explanation: Timbuktu was a major center of Islamic learning and scholarship, home to the famous University of Sankore and numerous manuscripts.

questions.question: The Suez Canal was opened in
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal was officially opened on November 17, 1869, connecting the Mediterranean and Red Seas.

questions.question: The Biafran War in Nigeria lasted from
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Civil War, also known as the Biafran War, lasted from July 6, 1967, to January 15, 1970.

questions.question: The Industrial Revolution began in
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the late 18th century before spreading to other parts of Europe and North America.

questions.question: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) was founded in
questions.explanation: The Organization of African Unity was founded on May 25, 1963, in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, to promote unity among African states.

questions.question: The French Revolution began in
questions.explanation: The French Revolution began in 1789 with the convening of the Estates-General and the storming of the Bastille on July 14, 1789.

questions.question: The Zulu Kingdom was founded by
questions.explanation: Shaka Zulu founded and expanded the Zulu Kingdom in the early 19th century, transforming it into a powerful military state.

questions.question: The United Nations was established in
questions.explanation: The United Nations was officially established on October 24, 1945, when the UN Charter came into force after World War II.

questions.question: The Apartheid system in South Africa was officially dismantled in
questions.explanation: Apartheid officially ended in 1994 with South Africa's first democratic elections, which brought Nelson Mandela to power.

questions.question: The Mongol Empire was founded by
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire in 1206, which became the largest contiguous land empire in history.

questions.question: The Rwandan Genocide occurred in
questions.explanation: The Rwandan Genocide took place over approximately 100 days from April to July 1994, resulting in the mass killing of Tutsi and moderate Hutu populations.
